alternatives: Cut the claim that data centres will heat Finland's climate: roughly 44 TWh a year of waste heat from 5 GW is negligible against solar input over 338000 km2. Local heat-island effects near a site are real; regional forcing is not. Cut the waste-heat-to-electricity feedback loop: data centre heat runs 15 to 70 C, typically about 38 C, and conversion at that grade is thermodynamically hopeless, which is exactly why district heating with heat pumps lifting to about 66 C is the right use. Replace sodium with the real options: two-phase immersion in dielectric fluids, direct-to-chip liquid loops, and supercritical CO2 Brayton cycles for the stop-boiling-water instinct. Move the water argument to Arizona, Texas, Spain and Chile, where it bites; Finland is water-rich and Hamina uses seawater.

text: Fingrid has fielded over 50,000 MW of datacenter connection inquiries, against Finnish peak consumption of roughly 15,000 MW
author: claude-code
rationale: Replaces an earlier figure of 24,000 MW of connection applications described as five times Finnish nuclear capacity. That framing traces to a pseudonymous Medium post and appears on no Fingrid page. Fingrid's own public numbers are larger and benchmark against peak consumption, not nuclear capacity. A second Fingrid source puts preliminary inquiries at 100 GW, six times peak consumption.
revisit: When Fingrid publishes an updated connection inquiry total
cost_if_wrong: The wrong number understates the pipeline by half and compares it to the wrong baseline. It shipped in googles-13-billion-in-finland and in four translations before correction.

text: Page treatment for the OpenJev post
author: claude-code
rationale: Owner wants it close to Plan A in colour and in how the page's animated components behave.
cost_if_wrong: The figure states are keyed to heading ids; a palette change is cheap, a structural change means redoing the state table.
choice: Plan A's paper typesetting (ET Book, --pa tokens, sidenotes via PlanAMarkdown) with oxide as the only accent, plus a scroll-linked leaderboard figure in the right rail. The figure merges the lab's Leaderboard and W&B variants. HF card and Kaggle variants rejected by the owner; Leaderboard and W&B liked for structure but not their colours.
alternatives: HF model card pastiche; Kaggle public/private competition page; W&B report in its own dark palette; Leaderboard site in dark with lime; ink-blue, pencil-green or site-gold accents.

text: Animation driver for the OpenJev board
author: claude-code
rationale: Twelve bars do not need WebGL; the blog's scroll-driven figures all use ScrollTrigger. The owner mentioned anime.js assuming Plan A used it; Plan A uses GSAP and R3F.
choice: SVG figure driven by GSAP ScrollTrigger, same pattern as the Plan A fence (state read from heading positions at 60% viewport).
alternatives: react-three-fiber; anime.js; framer-motion layout.
